# CRAM live session

The developer says what the robot does next. You write each step as a *cell*, show its code, perform it in a kernel that stays alive between steps, and report what happened. The kernel keeps the world, the robot, the simulation and every moment before a cell, so a step can be undone, retried or replayed in seconds instead of rebuilding the scene.

The data structures live in CRAM (`experiments.live_session`, and the snapshot of a stepped MuJoCo simulation in `semantic_digital_twin.adapters.multi_sim`); read them, and the actions and helpers a step needs, in the codebase. The scripts next to this file drive the kernel. Code you write in cells follows `@AGENTS.md` only loosely: cells are throwaway, but anything that proves itself moves into the codebase under the full rules.

## Working loop
<!-- from WorkingLoopRules in agent_skills.py -->
- **One step per instruction.** Do what the developer asked, then stop and wait. Never chain further robot steps on your own, even when the next one seems obvious. An instruction with several parts ("open the gripper, put a finger left of the lever, push right") is one step; perform its parts in one cell
- **Show the code before you perform it.** Every motion cell goes into the chat as a code block first, then gets performed. Measuring code may be summarised in a sentence
- **Report from the reports.** Every cell ends with `session.report(label=..., outcome=...)`; quote the status, measure where the robot got to when the step is about reaching somewhere, and say in a sentence what that means for the instruction (reached, stopped short by how much, what failed)
- **When a step fails, diagnose before retrying.** Measure with a raw run (what is near, which joint is at its limit, which body blocks) and offer the developer concrete options with a recommendation. Do not loop through blind retries
- **Undo instead of rebuilding.** To retry a step, `session.revert_last_cell()`; to show steps again, `session.replay(first_cell=i, namespace=globals())`. Name a checkpoint the developer will want to come back to with `session.take_snapshot(name=...)`
- **Keep the developer's words.** Cell titles say what the developer asked for, in their words; they are what the history shows

## Setting up
<!-- from SettingUpRules in agent_skills.py -->
- The kernel runs in a container with CRAM and MuJoCo on a server reachable by ssh. `scripts/live_kernel.py` drives it from this machine; run it with the project's Python interpreter. Every option of it defaults to the `LIVE_*` environment variable of the same name (`--server` to `LIVE_SERVER`), and the defaults fit the CRAM docker image (CRAM in `/opt/cram`, environment `/entrypoint.sh`)
- Ask the developer for `LIVE_SERVER`, `LIVE_CONTAINER` and `LIVE_EXCHANGE_ON_SERVER`, the server's side of a directory mounted into the container at `LIVE_EXCHANGE_IN_CONTAINER`
- `live_kernel.py start` starts the kernel in the container and runs `templates/robocasa_session.py` in it: that loads a RoboCasa kitchen with a PR2, starts the physics, defines `run(*actions) -> PlanOutcome` and creates `session` with a snapshot `composed`. For another scene or robot, copy the template to your scratchpad, change its first cell and pass it with `--template`
- If the kernel runs already, `start` leaves it alone; set the session up again with `live_kernel.py raw TEMPLATE`. After a kernel restart everything in it is gone, snapshots included

## Performing steps
<!-- from PerformingStepsRules in agent_skills.py -->
- Write the cell to a file in your scratchpad, starting with `# %% cell <title>` and ending with `session.report(label="...", outcome=outcome)`
- Perform it with `live_kernel.py perform FILE`, several cells of a file with `--cells 2:4`. The output streams back as the kernel prints it. A run still going after `LIVE_WAIT_SECONDS` keeps running; follow it with `live_kernel.py wait NAME`
- Use `live_kernel.py raw FILE` for measuring and for set up code: a raw run is not kept in the history, so replays do not repeat it
